blast_radius_definition: BR = |Gold rows deviating from clean reference (changed, missing or unexpected)| / |Gold rows in reference ∪ current|; CRASH -> 0 (ASSIGNED_CRASH)
key_findings: 6/14 faults corrupt Gold while the pipeline reports SUCCESS (silent propagation): M4a_NullAndNegative, M4b_NullSmall, M4c_DuplicateKeys, M5a_MULTIPLY_100, M5b_MULTIPLY_1_5, M5c_CATEGORICAL_SHIFT.
M5a (discount x100) and M5b (x1.5) each corrupt 175/190 Gold rows (BR 92.1%).
Even tiny injections propagate: M4b injects only 5 NULL keys yet changes 5 Gold rows; M4c (5 duplicate PKs) changes 8 rows.

All 3 type mutations are NEUTRALISED: Silver CASTs restore the type, so Gold is bit-identical. The schema contract is violated but data is not corrupted — a latent risk, not an observable failure (important for interpreting Detection Rate).
All 3 destructive mutations CRASH the pipeline: protection by accident, with no diagnosis of the root cause.
Additive mutations are harmless (explicit SELECT in Silver).
Gold-row BR understates severity for small injections because Gold is aggregated; report BR together with the binary 'propagated' outcome.

Benign mutations: FPR = 0/5 trivially (C0 raises no alarms). Some benign mutations legitimately change Gold (e.g. B2 value shift) — a value-diff alone cannot separate fault from benign, which motivates contract-based validation.
